chapter: Claude Hopkins, Fletcher Henderson and Fats Waller
title: Playing with Jelly Roll Morton
summary: Mosley works briefly upstate with Morton, who carried cash, after meeting him at the Rhythm Club.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Did you go with Fletcher right away?
You must have been getting around a little bit.
You didn't know Jelly Roll Morton, did you?
I played with Jelly Roll Morton.
I went with Jelly Roll Morton upstate and that was funny. He always walked around with a gang of hundred dollar bills in his pocket; he wouldn't be alive today if he was living.

Yeah, I was with Jelly Roll. I had to get with somebody. I met him at the Rhythm Club down here, and he had heard me play when I was with Claude and he said, you're not doing anything? I said I'm not; you are now.
That's the way he was. Then Fletcher had to go--that's when I went and joined Fletcher, but we only played Yale, Harvard--
